the noncanonical roles of telomeres and telomerase are not well defined and that they are still a matter of controversy.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the telomerase enzyme is not restricted to telomeres and that it has a wide variety of effects that are important for cell biology and cancer.
telomerase can be considered as a tumor suppressor or as an oncogene.

telomerase plays a role in many aspects of cell biology and that the extratelomere effects are important and might be the major cause of the tumor‐promoter activity of the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) in cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
telomerase, the enzyme responsible for the lengthening of telomeres, is not just a telomere‐targeted enzyme, but it also exerts effects that are independent of its role on the telomeres.
telomerase has many faces and that it has a much wider range of effects in the cell than previously thought.

telomerase has many functions in the cell, and that the functions that we are most familiar with (telomere length maintenance and immortalization of cancer cells) may not even be the most important ones.
